topHypothesis:
Hypothesis: Biofilms act as the structural and ecological driver that concentrates all three HGT mechanisms (conjugation, transduction, transformation) and the resistome in hospital environments by creating dense, DNA-rich microenvironments that favor gene exchange.
Mechanism: Biofilms provide high cell density, extracellular DNA accumulation, reduced diffusion, quorum-sensing competence induction, and protective matrices that stabilize donor-recipient proximity and protect free DNA and phages from degradation. These conditions simultaneously enhance conjugative cell contact, provide substrate for transformation, and sustain phage replication, making biofilms hotspots where resistome genes (from pathogenic, commensal, and environmental bacteria plus MGEs) can be mobilized into pathogens.

(observable: Per-unit-cell (or per-biofilm-volume) transfer frequency of antibiotic resistance genes via each of the three HGT mechanisms (conjugation, transduction, transformation) in established polymicrobial biofilms versus matched planktonic control cultures under identical antibiotic pressure and cell density.).

topHypothesis:
Hypothesis: Low tumor mutational burden and consequent low neoantigen load in mismatch repair-proficient CRC means too few mutation-derived neoantigens are presented to prime robust cytotoxic T-cell responses, leaving anti-PD-1/PD-L1 blockade without a sufficient antigen-driven T-cell pool to reactivate, so only high-TMB dMMR tumors respond.
Mechanism: Mutation-derived neoantigen presentation is the rate-limiting driver of the anti-tumor T-cell repertoire. In MSS tumors, low TMB yields sparse neoantigens, so the endogenous TCR repertoire lacks high-frequency tumor-reactive clones; checkpoint blockade removes PD-1-mediated inhibition but there are too few activated tumor-reactive T cells to produce a clinical response. In dMMR tumors, high TMB provides abundant neoantigens that generate a large, reactivatable T-cell pool.
Predictions: Across CRC patients, objective response to PD-1 blockade should correlate monotonically with nonsynonymous mutation count (or predicted neoantigen load) after controlling for MSI status. | Within the dMMR subset, non-responders should have measurably lower nonsynonymous mutation burdens than responders. | MSS tumors engineered to carry a dMMR-level mutation load (e.g., via induced hypermutation or neoantigen vaccines) should acquire responsiveness to checkpoint blockade.
Expected relation: ORR should increase monotonically with TMB/neoantigen load after controlling for MSI status. Within dMMR tumors, responders should have higher nonsynonymous mutation counts than non-responders, and MSS tumors should essentially never respond regardless of moderate elevations in TMB. (observable: Objective response rate (ORR) to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 blockade as a function of nonsynonymous mutation burden/TMB and neoantigen load in CRC, especially within the dMMR subset comparing responders vs. non-responders.).
